newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian shares edge lower in sluggish trade.
newsitem.headline: Russian shares edge lower in sluggish trade.

text.p: Leading Russian shares barely budged overall on Wednesday, although some rose on selective and limited demand, helping to couterbalance sales by long position holders.
The Russian Trading System 22-share index ended little changed at 363.96, down 0.4 percent from 365.26 on Tuesday.
Total volume was a paltry $26.8 million, and some traders attributed the sluggish pace of Wednesday's activity to players winding down ahead of the independence day holiday on Thursday.

Demand was strongest for shares in oil companies LUKoil LKOH.RTS and Surgutneftegaz SNGS.RTS, traders said, adding recent strong buying interest in Sberbank SBER.RTS shares waned slightly, although they held above $200.

"Sberbank pulled back slightly today," said UFG trader Igor Vine. "It is totally understandable given that the shares have gone up around 60 points so quickly and broke through the $200 barrier. Some consolidation is now needed."
He said that the fact that Sberbank shares had held above $200 despite Wednesday's small technical correction suggested the level would provide support in the future.
Sberbank shares closed at $204, down just $1 from Tuesday's settlement.
Traders said they saw continued demand for LUKoil shares, and buying interest in oil comapny Surgutneftegaz and its parent company NK Surgut Holding.

"Surgut Holding is moving up quite quickly, because of the lack of offers. LUKoil, having broken above $15.00 last week, gave a kickstart to another big oil firm, Surgutneftegaz, in the so-called domino effect," Vine said.
Shares in NK Surgut Holding are not traded on the RTS system, but over-the-counter and generally in very thin volume.
But Dmitry Konov, head analyst of securities operations at Bank MFK (ICFI), said the slow tempo of the rise in Surgutneftegaz shares meant it had seen the end of big rises.
Surgutneftegaz shares rose to $0.945 from $0.940, while LUKoil stayed unchanged at $15.60 per share.
Traders noted gains during the past two days in Aeroflot to $130 from $120 and in Bashinformsvyaz to $1.70 from $1.35.
Vine said there was talk on the market that a major western investors had already allocated funds to Russian shares.
"The only question remaining is which shares they invest in and how aggressively," he said.
